title: Service availability notice and recovery outline (customer-facing)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This file contains two polished, customer-facing artifacts you can copy into the status page, support emails, or account contacts: 1) a short status-page style availability/incident update for real-time use, and 2) a concise post-incident summary (executive + technical) intended for impacted customers after the incident is closed. Both are written to be accessible to product and engineering contacts at customer organizations while avoiding internal jargon.

How to use:
- Pick the appropriate status update template below for the current phase (detect/mitigate/recover/closed).
- Replace placeholder tokens in uppercase (e.g., <INCIDENT_ID>, <AFFECTED_REGIONS>, <MODEL_OR_FEATURE>) with incident-specific values.
- For any public status posts, do NOT include internal ticket numbers or unreconciled hypotheses (use the Confluence link in linked_artifacts for that).

Status page / short update templates (copyable snippets)
1) Initial acknowledgement (short)
Title: Service disruption affecting <MODEL_OR_FEATURE> in <AFFECTED_REGIONS>
Body: We are currently investigating elevated error rates and request failures for <MODEL_OR_FEATURE> affecting customers in <AFFECTED_REGIONS>. Our on-call and SRE teams are actively investigating. At this time, requests may see increased latency or errors (HTTP 5xx / timeouts). We will post another update within 30 minutes or when there is a material change. Incident ID: <INCIDENT_ID>.

2) Mitigation in progress
Title: Mitigation underway for <MODEL_OR_FEATURE> impact
Body: Our teams have identified a degraded subsystem related to <SHORT_ROOT_CAUSE_HINT, e.g. model routing/cache layer> and have applied a targeted mitigation to reduce error rates. Some customers may see intermittent successes as the mitigation propagates. We continue to monitor and are preparing a follow-up with impact metrics and next steps within 60 minutes.

3) Recovery notice (user guidance)
Title: Partial recovery — service returning to normal for most customers
Body: We have applied a fix and are observing request success rates returning to normal for the majority of traffic in <AFFECTED_REGIONS>. If you continue to see errors, please: 
- Retry requests with exponential backoff (recommended: 500ms -> 1s -> 2s)
- If you use pinned model variants, consider temporarily switching to <FALLBACK_MODEL> if you require immediate throughput
- Contact support@redwood-inference.example with logs and request IDs indicated in the error response.
We will publish a full incident summary once root cause verification and follow-up actions are complete.

4) Closure confirmation (short)
Title: Incident resolved — <MODEL_OR_FEATURE> available
Body: The incident affecting <MODEL_OR_FEATURE> in <AFFECTED_REGIONS> has been resolved as of <RESOLUTION_TIMESTAMP>. We have validated normal request success and latency for representative customers. A post-incident summary is being prepared and will be shared here and with affected account contacts.

Customer-facing post-incident summary template (concise, to send after verification)
Header: Post-incident summary — <INCIDENT_ID> (affecting <MODEL_OR_FEATURE>)
1) Executive summary (2-3 sentences):
On <START_TIMESTAMP> we observed a service disruption affecting requests to <MODEL_OR_FEATURE> in <AFFECTED_REGIONS>, causing elevated error rates and increased latency for X% of customer traffic. The issue was resolved at <RESOLUTION_TIMESTAMP>, and normal service has been confirmed. We recognize the impact and apologize for the disruption.

2) Impact (bullet list):
- Scope: <NUMBER_OF_CUSTOMERS> accounts experienced failures; <AFFECTED_REGIONS> were primarily impacted.
- Symptoms: increased 5xx error rate, timeouts, and intermittent token-level truncation for some requests.
- Duration: <ELAPSED_TIME> from detection to resolution.
- Severity: production availability impact; customer SLA windows that overlapped the incident may be eligible for credits per contract.

3) Root cause (summary, customer-friendly):
A component responsible for routing requests to model-serving pools experienced a configuration regression during a capacity routing change. This caused a subset of requests to be directed to a degraded cluster variant, which resulted in sustained errors and cache misses.

4) Mitigation and resolution (what we did):
- Immediate: rolled back the routing change and applied an isolation rule to divert traffic from the degraded pool.
- Short-term: restarted affected serving nodes and increased routing retries to reduce failed handoffs.
- Verification: synthetic and customer production traffic checks indicate success metrics (error rate, tail latency) returned to baseline.

5) Customer actions and workarounds (if applicable):
- Retry failed requests with standard retry/backoff.
- If you rely on pinned resources, consider allowing a temporary fallback to <FALLBACK_MODEL> until we finalize rebalancing.
- For long-running jobs, requeue requests where possible.

6) Follow-up and long-term fixes (planned):
- Full postmortem with detailed timeline and telemetry will be published to Confluence (link above).
- Persistent fix: add pre-deployment routing canaries and stricter config validation to prevent similar regressions.
- Observability: we will add a dedicated alert for cross-pool cache-miss spikes and increase retention on the affected tracing keys for 30 days.
- Compensation: customers with SLA impacted windows will be contacted by your account lead to discuss credits where applicable.

7) Ownership and contacts:
- Incident lead: <INCIDENT_LEAD_NAME> (oncall)
- Customer success contact: <CS_LEAD_NAME> (direct email)
- Support: support@redwood-inference.example (provide request IDs and timestamps)

Sample full-body email for account teams (slightly more detailed than the status page)
Subject: Post-incident summary — <INCIDENT_ID> — Impact to <MODEL_OR_FEATURE> on <START_DATE>
Body:
Hello <ACCOUNT_TEAM/CONTACT>,

We’re writing to summarize the incident that affected <MODEL_OR_FEATURE> on <START_DATE>. Executive summary: <2-3 sentence executive summary>

Impact:
- Affected: <NUMBER_OF_CUSTOMERS> customers in <AFFECTED_REGIONS>
- Symptoms: elevated 5xx, timeouts; downstream retries may have increased customer request costs.
- Window: <START_TIMESTAMP> to <RESOLUTION_TIMESTAMP>

Root cause and what we did:
- Root cause: <COMPONENT> configuration regression during a routing update led to traffic being sent to a degraded variant.
- Fix: rolled back change, isolated degraded pool, restarted nodes, validated with canary traffic.

Next steps and mitigations we are implementing:
- Short-term: extend fallback routing for 72 hours, add temporary throttling on background rebalances.
- Long-term: improved pre-deploy checks, additional canary capacity, and a guardrail in the control plane.

We’re sorry for the disruption. If you want a technical deep-dive call with our SRE and serving runtime leads, reply and we’ll schedule.

Best,
<CS_LEAD_NAME> on behalf of Redwood Inference

Customer-sensitive phrasing guidance (do’s and don’ts)
Do:
- Be transparent about what customers saw and when.
- Offer clear remediation steps and a point of contact.
- Avoid internal ticket hashes or unverified causes in customer posts.
- If you don’t yet know root cause, say ‘under investigation’ and commit to a follow-up time.

Don’t:
- Use internal-only shorthand (e.g., ‘cache hotfix v3’) or include sensitive internal metrics.
- Promise timelines for fixes you cannot control (e.g., hardware replacements).

Quick copy snippets for Slack/email to execs/account leads
- Short incident alert (for account channel):  "ALERT: <INCIDENT_ID> — <MODEL_OR_FEATURE> experiencing elevated errors in <AFFECTED_REGIONS>. SRE oncall investigating. CS lead: <CS_LEAD_NAME>. We'll update in 30 mins."
- Postmortem summary snippet: "Resolved <INCIDENT_ID> — root cause: routing config regression; fix: rollback + isolation; next: canary gating and config validation. Account leads notified for SLA review."

Internal notes for CS lead when preparing customer outreach
- Confirm the list of impacted accounts (Jira filter: JIRA-INC-4827 IMPACTED-ACCOUNTS).
- Validate the exact error signatures customers will see (sample request IDs: list).
- Coordinate with SRE for a one-pager with timelines and telemetry graphs for customers who request deeper detail.
- Decide on proactive offer to schedule a technical call for top X accounts.

Version history and approvals
- Drafted by: Ava Martinez (Customer Success)
- Technical review: Rajesh Nair (SRE), Emily Chen (Serving Runtime)
- Communication review: Marcus Li (Legal)

Notes: keep public status page posts concise; use the post-incident summary for emailed follow-ups to affected accounts. Always attach or link to the Confluence postmortem for customers that request detailed telemetry or timelines.
